It was a store where you were struck by the exterior before entering, the interior when entering, and the smell when you sat down.

The interior of the store was cute and cozy. The disappointing thing is that it is small, with only 3 tables, and the total number of guests that can be accommodated seems to be limited to 7 people.

The star rating was very high, but I thought it would be great if the dessert was delicious, so I think it was worth the high rating. The owner seems to be baking the scones in real time in his small shop, so the fragrant smell fills the air quickly, and the scones are not dry, but soft on the inside and crispy on the outside. I wonder if this is what it looks like on the outside and inside.

I wondered what it would have been like to drink coffee while eating Injeolmi scones, but I promised myself next time. But I think it was really worth eating.

If you like scones, this is a recommended store.

reviews.author: Chalney
reviews.text:
A unique tteokbokki restaurant where the food is friendly and the owner is delicious (!)

Food: The tteokbokki was more generous than expected. It comes with a variety of noodles, dumplings, and quail eggs inside, and a lot of fried vegetables on top. Tteokbokki is a type of soup that is not too thick and is spicy rather than sweet. It was unusual to have seaweed in it, but it was edible. The tempura doesn't seem to be homemade; it's just regular, clean tempura. I was disappointed that the vegetable tempura batter seemed a little undercooked. It seemed like the sundae was also being used as a prototype.

Service: The owner is very friendly! I really enjoyed the bean cream served as a service :) Candy was also prepared for dessert. The store is clean and they seem to be very careful about hygiene...!!

Personally, it wasn't my favorite type of tteokbokki, but I recommend it to those who like less sweet soup tteokbokki.

It is located about 5-10 minutes away from Konkuk University Entrance Line 2. Is there a cafe here? It's located near the bus stop, and when you see the cafe guide sign next to it, you can go inside. It feels like a remodeled home. All you have to do is open the door and enter.

The inside was bigger than I expected, and the counter was directly visible, and desserts were displayed separately inside, so the system was to bring them to the counter and purchase them. I visited because I wanted to drink coffee, so I didn't look at the other drink menu, but I guess it would be diverse.

There was no separate filter type, and you could choose the coffee beans when ordering coffee. Fritz coffee beans were used and there were two types of coffee beans: Old Dog, which was the most popular, and Jajjae Gasina. As expected, the coffee was delicious. I additionally ordered pudding and bean butter, which were both very delicious.

The interior was also well decorated. The lighting felt warm and the dishes were pretty. The seats weren't comfortable, but it didn't feel that uncomfortable either.

Although the location is a bit ambiguous, I was thankful that there was a cafe like this here. If I want to drink delicious coffee on my way to or from work, I should visit again.

It may seem expensive compared to its size, but it is rich and delicious.
I like dacquoise en butter and chocolate madeleine🥰🥰 It's so delicious.
In particular, the madeleine is not just a chocolate bread, but also has shell-shaped chocolate attached to it, so the chewy texture of the chocolate and the soft texture of the madeleine go well together, making it even more delicious!!! Iced Americano is perfect for the size!! LOL

Once you go, you will always remember it!!
I recommend it!!
